title: Geofence topologies and failover playbook for regional dedicated fleets
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Define product requirements and rollout plan for regional "geofence" topologies and deterministic failover for Dedicated fleets. The doc covers placement policy primitives, autoscaling templates that respect throughput guarantees and per-customer data residency constraints, deterministic failover sequencing across zones and regions, console UX changes, and telemetry/SLAs to validate behavior.
background: Several enterprise customers require: (a) strict residency for inference traffic and KV backups, (b) throughput guarantees under reserved capacity, and (c) predictable failover semantics across regions/zones for DR exercises. Current Dedicated controls expose basic zone affinity and capacity pools but lack prescriptive topology templates and an operator playbook for safe failover while preserving residency and SLOs.
goals: Ship a set of topology templates (single-zone, active-active regional, regional-hot-standby) for Dedicated fleets
Provide autoscaling policy presets that balance throughput guarantees (reserved qps/token budget) with cost and locality
Define deterministic failover sequences that preserve data residency where required
Surface residency and topology at provisioning time in Console + API; add rollout guardrails and telemetry
non_goals: Implementing full cross-region synchronous replication for model weights (engineering workstream)
Changing billing model for reserved capacity within this ticket
Addressing on-prem air-gapped install mechanics (covered in Private roadmap separately)
acceptance_criteria: Topology templates available as selectable options in API and Console when creating Dedicated fleets
Autoscaling presets documented and deployable; operators can toggle between 'throughput-guaranteed' and 'cost-priority' modes
Failover playbook automated steps implemented as a CLI/API runbook for canary and full failover with clear rollback paths
Telemetry exposes: per-fleet residency compliance flag, failover events timeline, pre/post failover latency and token throughput metrics
Security review completed and export controls validated for residency-bound traffic
proposed_solution_summary: Introduce geofence-aware fleet topologies and three autoscaling policy presets. Topologies encode placement intent and residency constraints; autoscaling policies respect reserved throughput budgets while allowing emergency cross-zone burst within residency bounds. Implement a deterministic failover coordinator that executes staged failover steps (zone -> regional -> cross-region) with automated KV prefix migration and a traffic-engineered ramp-down/ramp-up plan to avoid transient SLO violations.
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (internal beta): Expose topology templates in API; run against test fleets and synthetic traffic (Mar 2026)
Phase 2 (customer alpha): 3 pilot customers under NDA, exercise DR runbooks and gather telemetry (Apr 2026)
Phase 3 (general availability): Console UI, autoscaling policy presets, docs, and SDK examples; enable opt-in for existing Dedicated customers (May 2026)
Phase 4 (post-GA): Add advisory checks and automated canary failovers as a managed feature (Q3 2026)
metrics: Fraction of Dedicated fleets created using a topology template
Percent of failovers that preserve residency constraints
Throughput compliance rate vs reserved guarantees during failover
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Cross-region failover could violate legal residency obligations. Mitigation: enforce residency flag that blocks cross-region traffic unless customer explicitly allows temporary exception
Risk: Automated failover triggers might cause cascading autoscale churn. Mitigation: coordinator uses quorum-based gating + cooling windows and reserve token buckets for steady-state throughput
Risk: Increased operator complexity in Console. Mitigation: provide curated presets and descriptive inline docs; run UX testing during alpha
Risk: Telemetry gaps. Mitigation: add pre/post snapshot hooks for KV caches and token routing logs as part of failover sequence
open_questions: What is the legal definition of "data residency" we must enforce vs. recommended locality? (Legal input required)
Should we allow customer-configured 'temporary cross-region exception' with time-bounded audit logging?
How to price cross-region burst that occurs only during failover? Fixed surcharge or metered on tokens?
Do we require synchronous confirmation of KV prefix transfer before routing traffic, or is eventual consistency acceptable for some customers?
